create_provider.note: metadataXml is a proto bytes field — value MUST be base64-encoded. Use metadataUrl as simpler alternative. For mock-idp: metadataUrl MUST be 'http://mock-idp:9090/saml/metadata' (NOT /metadata).

enable_auth_method.note: ownerType MUST be exactly 'IDP_OWNER_TYPE_ORG' (protobuf enum). NOT 'ORG', 'OWNER_TYPE_ORG', or 'org'. Requires org-level login policy to exist first.

update_application.note: Updates the org-level login policy. Use this to enable external IdP login (allowExternalIdp=true).

saml.description: ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flows when acting as a SAML provider/broker.
saml.note: IdP-initiated attempts failing are by design and should not be flagged as flow-coherence issues.

saml.description: The SAML SSO endpoint returns HTTP 200 even when the SAML response contains an error StatusCode.
saml.note: Use SAML protocol status or downstream OIDC completion, not HTTP status alone, as the oracle.

saml.description: ZITADEL issues opaque access tokens by default rather than JWTs.
saml.note: Tests that expect JWT claims in access_token must either introspect or explicitly request/configure JWT tokens.

saml.description: When requesting an ID token via token exchange, the returned token is placed in the access_token field and token_type is N_A.
saml.note: This looks odd but is RFC-aligned behavior; do not use that value as a Bearer token for API calls.

saml.description: When token exchange requests an ID token, the returned ID token is placed in the access_token field and token_type is N_A.
saml.note: This looks malformed to generic OAuth tooling but is documented RFC 8693 behavior on this platform.

saml.description: Token introspection only reports active=true when the introspecting client is part of the token audience.
saml.note: An inactive introspection result can reflect audience mismatch rather than token expiry or revocation.

saml.description: Token exchange may legitimately return a token with scope different from the supplied token when requested and validated.
saml.note: Scope changes during token exchange are by design; only scopes exceeding documented authorization semantics should be flagged.

saml.description: ZITADEL uses opaque access tokens by default rather than JWTs.
saml.note: Tests must not assume access_token is locally parseable JWT; use userinfo or introspection for verification.

saml.constraint: ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flows. The fuzzer MUST initiate login through ZITADEL first and only then POST the forged SAMLResponse to the callback. IdP-initiated SAML tests are invalid on this platform and will fail by design.

For SAML signature-validation default tests (saml_cert_substitution, saml_unsigned_assertion, saml_spurious_signature), the executor MUST use the external IdP callback path /idps/callback and preserve the SP-initiated flow state. Sending a standalone fabricated SAMLResponse without first initiating the flow will be rejected for missing request context rather than for the security property under test.

SAML SSO endpoint /saml/v2/SSO returns HTTP 200 even on protocol errors; failure is encoded inside the SAML StatusCode/message. Do NOT use raw HTTP status from that endpoint as the oracle for SAML acceptance or rejection.

For I2 SAML replay and expiry tests, include a CONTROL brokered login first using the same provider configuration but without the attack mutation. Otherwise a failed forged SAML login cannot be distinguished from broken provider setup, missing attribute mapping, or disabled external IdP login policy.

ZITADEL user creation from external SAML IdPs may fail unless required attributes are mapped via Actions V2 on /zitadel.user.v2.UserService/RetrieveIdentityProviderIntent. For SAML login tests that expect successful first-time federation, the fuzzer MUST ensure the upstream assertion provides required fields and that the instance is configured to map them; otherwise login failure is expected setup failure, not a security rejection.

External IdP login must be enabled in the login policy. If 'External Login allowed' is disabled at instance/org level, all SAML broker logins will fail regardless of assertion validity. The fuzzer MUST enable this before interpreting login failures as security outcomes.

If organization-specific login settings override defaults, the authorization request MUST include the reserved organization scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id}; otherwise ZITADEL may apply default settings and select a different set of external IdPs. This is essential for tenant-isolated SAML tests and cross-org comparisons.

Token exchange audience is restrictive: requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. Cross-audience or cross-tenant token-exchange tests MUST first obtain subject/actor tokens whose audiences already include the target audience; otherwise rejection is by design.

Token exchange scope can differ from the input token and ZITADEL may extend or decrease scope based on validation. For I5 scope-escalation tests, compare the exchanged token's actual returned scope and claims, not merely whether the request was accepted.

When requested_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token in token exchange, ZITADEL returns the ID token in the access_token field and sets token_type=N_A. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat that returned access_token value as a bearer API credential.

ZITADEL rejects expired ID tokens used as subject_token in token exchange. For freshness tests involving token exchange with id_token subject tokens, expired-token rejection is by design and should not be interpreted as a broader replay defense beyond documented validation.

The token introspection endpoint reports active=true only if the requesting client is part of the token audience. For verification, the fuzzer MUST introspect with a client/application that is in the token audience; otherwise inactive/401 can be caused by audience mismatch rather than token invalidity.

ZITADEL opaque access tokens are the default token type. The fuzzer MUST use session_token=access_token for subsequent Bearer calls and may need introspection rather than local JWT parsing. Do not assume access tokens are JWTs unless the application is configured for JWT token type or token exchange requested JWT.

For OIDC authorization requests, nonce is mandatory for implicit flow and recommended for code flow. For brokered SAML logins that end in OIDC tokens, the fuzzer SHOULD send nonce and MUST validate nonce-dependent tests only in flows where nonce was actually supplied.

For OIDC code exchange, redirect_uri must exactly match the redirect_uri used in the authorization request. Any mismatch causes invalid_grant-style failure unrelated to SAML broker security properties.

JWT client assertions used for token or introspection authentication have strict freshness: iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour, aud MUST include ZITADEL issuing domain, and kid header is required to identify the key. Failures here are client-auth setup errors, not token-exchange or introspection security outcomes.

Reserved scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} enforces that the user is a member of the selected organization. Multi-tenant SAML tests using this scope MUST provision membership accordingly; otherwise login failure is expected authorization behavior, not an identity-binding bug.

Reserved audience scopes urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:{projectid}:aud and urn:zitadel:iam:org:project:id:zitadel:aud explicitly add project IDs to the access-token audience. For I5 audience-binding tests, the fuzzer MUST control these scopes carefully because omitted scopes can make a target audience absent by configuration rather than by enforcement.
ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flow. Any SAML test must first initiate a SAML request and obtain a request ID before finalization; IdP-initiated SAML tests are invalid on this platform.

SAML login in custom/programmatic flows is not a direct ACS POST of SAMLResponse. The documented API flow is: proxy/initiate SAML request -> GET /v2/saml/saml_requests/{id} if needed -> authenticate user via session APIs -> POST /v2/saml/saml_requests/{id} with session.sessionId and session.sessionToken. Do NOT assume a documented ACS endpoint that accepts attacker-supplied SAMLResponse exists in the provided docs.

The SAML SSO endpoint /saml/v2/SSO returns HTTP 200 even on SAML protocol errors; failure is indicated inside the SAML StatusCode/message, not by HTTP status. Do not treat HTTP 200 from SAML SSO as successful authentication.
For SAML brokered logins that end in OIDC tokens, verification must use access_token at /oidc/v1/userinfo. session_token must map to access_token, not id_token.

When testing token freshness or SAML-brokered login failures, include a control flow with a valid token/code/session. Otherwise a failed attack flow may be caused by broken setup rather than security enforcement.

Token exchange audience narrowing is enforced: requested audience must be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. Cross-audience or cross-tenant escalation tests must expect rejection when audience is not already present upstream.
Token exchange resource parameter is not supported and always results in invalid_target. Do not use resource to model audience tests on ZITADEL.

When requested_token_type is id_token in token exchange, the returned ID token is placed in access_token and token_type is N_A. Do NOT use that value as a Bearer token for verify_granted_identity or API access tests.

ZITADEL currently rejects expired ID tokens even when used as subject_token in token exchange. Expired-token exchange failures are by design and must not be interpreted as replay protection beyond documented validation.

For impersonation token-exchange tests, actor_token is required for subject_token_type urn:zitadel:params:oauth:token-type:user_id and for self-signed JWT subject tokens. Sending only a user_id or self-signed JWT as subject_token is invalid setup.
OIDC authorization requests should include state and nonce; nonce is mandatory for implicit flow. Nonce-related replay tests must use flows where nonce is actually expected and validated.

For private_key_jwt authentication, aud in the client assertion JWT must include ZITADEL's issuing domain and iat must not be older than 1 hour; kid header must identify the registered key. Failures outside these bounds are setup errors, not security findings.

Introspection returns active=true only if the token is active and the requesting client is part of the token audience. Audience-mismatch introspection failures are expected and should not be treated as token invalidity alone.

If organization-specific login settings override defaults, the authorization request must include scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id}; otherwise tests may hit default IdP/login policy instead of the intended organization configuration.

ZITADEL user creation from external SAML IdPs in Login V2 can fail unless required attributes are mapped via Actions V2 on /zitadel.user.v2.UserService/RetrieveIdentityProviderIntent. SAML broker tests that rely on just-in-time user creation must ensure required fields like email, first name, and last name are populated.

ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flows. The fuzzer MUST initiate the brokered login through the SP/OIDC side first and only then submit the forged SAMLResponse to /idps/callback. IdP-initiated standalone SAMLResponse tests are invalid on this platform and will produce false negatives for I1/I2/I5.

For all SAML broker tests, saml_login MUST preserve the SP-initiated flow state (request/query parameters and matching InResponseTo/RelayState). The JWT IdP documentation explicitly warns that proxied requests must keep all original query parameters intact to preserve critical OIDC flow state; the same browser-mediated broker statefulness applies to external IdP flows. Dropping state causes failures unrelated to the tested invariant (I3).

SAML broker login in ZITADEL completes into OIDC/OAuth tokens. A valid SAML test sequence MUST include the downstream OIDC steps: start_oidc_auth to initiate login, saml_login to satisfy the external IdP callback, and exchange_code_for_token to obtain the Bearer access token used by verify_granted_identity. Treating saml_login itself as returning an API session token is incorrect.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution tests, ZITADEL documentation states SAML trust is established via exchanged metadata/certificates and best practices require validating signatures and parties. The fuzzer MUST create/use a SAML provider with explicit metadata/certificate trust material and then submit a forged SAMLResponse signed by an attacker key. Acceptance would indicate trust-anchor failure; rejection is expected when provider trust is configured.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch tests, the fuzzer MUST vary the assertion Issuer/entity ID while keeping the rest of the flow valid. ZITADEL documentation describes issuer/entity ID as part of SAML trust and metadata exchange; mismatched issuer should be rejected. Do not interpret generic flow/setup failures as issuer validation.

For I2 saml_assertion_id_replay and saml_one_time_use_replay tests, use TWO saml_login events within independently initiated valid SP flows but reuse the same Assertion/@ID via fixed_assertion_id. ZITADEL SAML docs recommend historical cache / duplicate ID rejection as best practice. A second acceptance after a successful first login indicates replay weakness; a first-call failure invalidates the test.

For I2 saml_expired_assertion tests, include a CONTROL broker login with a non-expired assertion in the same environment before the expired assertion attempt. Without a successful control, rejection of the expired assertion cannot be distinguished from broken provider setup, missing attribute mapping, or disabled external IdP login policy.

For I5 saml_no_conditions and saml_no_audience_restriction tests, first establish a working baseline with a normal assertion. ZITADEL documentation lists Conditions, audience, destination, recipient, issuer, and validation window as required SAML validation best practices. Acceptance of assertions missing Conditions/Audience after baseline success is security-relevant; baseline failure is not.

Organization scoping affects which external IdPs are shown/used. If an organization overrides default settings, the authorization request MUST include scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id}; otherwise ZITADEL uses default settings and the intended SAML provider may not be selected. Missing org scope can cause false negatives in all SAML broker tests.

External IdP login must be enabled in the applicable login policy before SAML tests. If 'External Login allowed' is not enabled on the instance default or target organization, SAML broker login will fail by design. The fuzzer MUST treat this as setup failure, not as a security oracle.

For Login V2 SAML provider tests that create users just-in-time, required user fields may be absent unless an Action maps SAML attributes into ZITADEL user fields. The docs state user creation will fail unless required fields are set via Actions V2 on /zitadel.user.v2.UserService/RetrieveIdentityProviderIntent. The fuzzer MUST ensure attribute mapping exists or use identities whose attributes satisfy creation requirements; otherwise login failures are non-security-related.

SAML attribute values used for JIT provisioning are commonly multi-valued arrays in provider raw information (for example email, firstName, lastName arrays in the documented Actions examples). For I4 type-confusion and binding tests, the fuzzer SHOULD account for array-valued attributes versus scalar assumptions; failures may stem from mapping logic rather than broker identity binding.

Token exchange audience is restrictive by design: requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. Cross-project or cross-organization audience expansion attempts that fail are expected behavior, not I5 violations. Only acceptance of a new audience outside that combined set is security-relevant.

Token exchange scope can intentionally differ from the input token scope. ZITADEL documentation explicitly says scope can be used to extend or decrease the scope of the new token, subject to validation. Therefore, requesting a broader scope and receiving it is not automatically an I5 violation unless it exceeds upstream authorization intent or broker policy. The oracle MUST compare against documented token-exchange semantics, not assume monotonic narrowing.

When requested_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token in token exchange, the returned ID token is placed in the access_token field and token_type is N_A. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat that value as a Bearer session_token for subsequent API calls. For session-bearing follow-up calls, request an access token or JWT token type instead.

ZITADEL rejects expired ID tokens used as subject_token in token exchange. For I2 freshness tests involving token exchange, expired subject ID tokens should fail by design. Use a valid control token first to distinguish freshness enforcement from broken client authentication or grant configuration.

The token introspection endpoint returns active=true only if the token is active AND the requesting client is part of the token audience. Therefore, introspection failures can be caused by audience mismatch of the introspecting client rather than token invalidity. The fuzzer MUST use an introspecting client that is in the token audience before drawing I2/I5 conclusions.

ZITADEL access tokens are opaque by default. The fuzzer MUST use the returned access_token as the Bearer credential and rely on /oidc/v1/userinfo or /oauth/v2/introspect for verification rather than assuming local JWT parsing will work. Using id_token as the session credential is incorrect.

For OIDC authorization requests, nonce is mandatory for implicit flow and recommended for code flow to bind the client session and mitigate replay. Any I2 nonce-related test must include nonce in the authorization request and compare downstream ID token behavior accordingly; omitting nonce in implicit flow yields invalid setup rather than a broker vulnerability.

Client-authenticated calls to /oauth/v2/token, /oauth/v2/introspect, and /oauth/v2/revoke may use either client_secret_basic or private_key_jwt. For tests that depend on client authentication semantics, do not mix multiple client authentication mechanisms in one request; the token endpoint documents invalid_request/invalid_client for malformed or multiple credentials.

For private_key_jwt client authentication, the assertion aud MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain, iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour, and the JWT header MUST contain kid identifying the registered key. Failures from violating these requirements are setup errors, not security oracles.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: Zitadel management API uses REST gateway paths under /management/v1/ (org-scoped). Do NOT use gRPC Connect paths. For IdP setup: create_provider creates the IdP, enable_auth_method adds it to the login policy with ownerType='IDP_OWNER_TYPE_ORG' (NOT 'ORG' or 'OWNER_TYPE_ORG'). Both are needed before IdP login works. SAML login is brokered — saml_login is NOT directly callable as a standalone POST. It is handled internally by the executor's ZITADEL-LOGIN flow triggered via start_oidc_auth with scope containing urn:zitadel:iam:org:idp:id:{idp_id}.
